Real photographs vs. generated-at-runtime

Static preview only — no animation, no lighting rig, just the two candidate surfaces side by side so the choice is easy to make. Both columns get the same fake directional shading overlay so it's an apples-to-apples read on surface detail, not lighting.

Real texture (CC BY 4.0, NASA imagery)
Procedural (canvas, generated at load)
Earthday map
Marsstand-in for a planet flown past
Saturnreal ring texture, radially resampled
Sunself-lit, no shading pass
Recommendation: real textures, left column. At sphere sizes this small the procedural version reads as "blotchy gradient," not "planet" — the gap gets more obvious once GPU-lit and rotating in three.js, not less.
